seal.statement: The pre-push gate proves a push by its change: its test stage runs the change proof CI runs (the safety spine plus the changed subsystems, their witnesses and, for changed test support code, every test whose import closure reaches it) against the remote base the hook already receives, and runs the whole corpus only when the change proof cannot stand for it (a refused selection, a change to the selection machinery, runner, hook or package manifests, a cone above half the corpus, no committed range, or the operator asking); the whole corpus still runs on main after every push in a non-gating canary workflow; and the corpus ratchets run in place inside the exact-HEAD worktree instead of materialising a second one.

text: Lean push gate: (1) scripts/checks/helper-import-closure.js + selector change - changed non-test JS under test/ or src/test-helpers/ selects every classified test whose import closure reaches it from the sealed import graph, on top of its taxonomy subsystem; no sealed graph refuses with the regeneration hint; ordinary source never reads the graph. (2) scripts/checks/push-gate-change-proof.js - the postpush manifest's last command: runs the npm test plan against LAGRANGE_CHECK_BASE (the hook now exports the remote sha of main from the pushed-ref line), or test:all when refused, a selection-machinery/runner/state/hook/package path changed, the cone exceeds half the corpus, no committed range, or LAGRANGE_PUSH_FULL_CORPUS=1; decision is a pure exported function. (3) hook runs the corpus ratchets in place (--in-place) inside the exact-HEAD worktree. (4) safety spine += changed-paths, taxonomy, publish-head, and the two new tests. (5) ci.yml prepares the sealed import graph before the ordinary proof. (6) full-corpus-canary.yml: test:all on push to main, non-required, no schedule, cancel-in-progress. Docs: runbook, harness.md, hook header. Constants moved to change-selection-constants.js for the literal guideline.

Design review (independent subagent, 2026-09-12) verdicts implemented: step 1 ADOPT WITH CHANGES (replace only manifest command 6; feed LAGRANGE_CHECK_BASE from the pushed ref; close the fixture hole via the sealed import graph; full-corpus fallback triggers; spine additions; a non-gating full-corpus lane; expect 6-10 min publishes, not 3-4). Step 2 ADOPT at per-test-FILE granularity, local-only first: declared as quest test-file-content-receipts (unsealed; its probe script does not exist yet). Review premise correction recorded: CI does NOT run the full corpus after a push - ci.yml runs the same cone; repository-health refuses behavioural suites; test:all ran only in full-gate.yml - so without the canary the first full run would be the release proof.

Risks carried (review ranking): (1) without the canary, cone-hidden reds accumulate until the release proof - canary added, non-required; (2) exclusive-lane cones now run locally for the first time under the 120 s TAP floor - keep LAGRANGE_RETRY_FAILED_ONCE=1 in the gate, watch for thermal false reds; (3) the import graph only sees imports: a fixture read through fs (JSON, SQL) still widens only to test-infrastructure - known v1 limit, the receipts quest's blanket non-JS invalidation is the same boundary; (4) red-main attribution is per push (CI proves before..HEAD), bisecting stays manual; (5) full-corpus canary on a hosted runner may be noisy for cluster tests - it gates nothing, so noise costs attention, not landings.

Corrective (verifier round 1 REJECT): selection-state trigger narrowed to curated state only (safety-spine.json, impact-contracts.json, test/manifests/); the import-graph seal and the generated census manifests are ordinary (measured: the seal alone would have run the corpus on 17 of 60 pushes); package.json/lockfile dropped from the triggers - the selector is the one authority on their meaning; hook: the pushed ref's remote sha wins over an ambient LAGRANGE_CHECK_BASE (announced); ci.yml fails loudly on a stale committed seal instead of silently widening; canary timeout 300 min with the hosted-runner speed noted; closure header states the v1 import-edge scope; --explain exit comment. Path-trigger census over the last 60 origin/main commits after the fix: see log.

Path-trigger census over the last 60 origin/main commits (fullCorpusTriggers only; refused/size/no-range not counted): with the seal and package rules 45/60 would have run the corpus (verifier); seal excluded and package dropped: 13/60 (selection-state 14 hits, machinery 8, runner 4 - a fortnight dominated by two process quests editing impact-contracts.json and the gate manifests, so the steady-state share should be lower). Measure again after ten ordinary landings.

Corrective (verifier round 2 advisory 1): the gate's import closure is now asserted in test/scripts/push-gate-change-proof.test.js (static relative imports from the nine gate entry points; every reached module must trip a trigger); the five it found are covered - impact-proof-cone-constants.js and test-timeout-declarations.js under selection-machinery, and a classification-generator rule for the three generate-test-*-classes.js. Advisory 2 (package.json scripts edits widen, shapes pinned by spine contract tests) accepted as designed.

Corrective (verifier round 3 advisories): the closure test now starts from the scheduler too (run-project-hardening-acceptance.js, acceptance-proof-manifest-runner.js) and catches bare side-effect imports; a gate-scheduler trigger covers the scheduler, the manifest runner and its constants module.

Independent verifier, four rounds: r1 REJECT (selection-state trigger matched the import-graph seal - 45/60 pushes would have run the corpus; fixed, census 13/60), r2 APPROVE with advisories (gate closure had five untriggered modules; fixed with a closure-derived spine assertion), r3 APPROVE with advisories (scheduler outside the closure, side-effect imports; fixed), r4 APPROVE: 25 gate modules reached from eleven entry points, 0 untriggered; cross-checked against the sealed import graph; hook ref parsing, base export precedence, in-place ratchets, manifest wiring, canary contract, docs and guideline audits verified; residual risks recorded (canary completion under cancel-in-progress on a hosted runner; package.json scripts edits prove via spine-pinned script shapes).

Altitude check after four attempts: one build plus three verifier-driven corrections, each narrowing or self-checking the full-corpus trigger list rather than widening the change; the quest statement is met (probe 0, change proof 149/149 green, r4 approval). No sign of chasing: the corrections converged on a closure-derived assertion that makes the class of drift a spine failure. Land.
